letter.subject: Tesla FSD Supervised — please take a public position on the TCMV vote
letter.sigVehicle: [I own a Hardware 4 Tesla / I own a Hardware 3 Tesla, which I understand is outside the current approval / I do not own a Tesla]
letter.clauseDE: Germany has said the KBA is assessing the file
letter.clauseES: Spain has said it prefers coordination with the Commission rather than a unilateral copy of the Dutch approval
letter.clauseFR: Minister Tabarot declined national recognition of the current product on 22 July 2026.
letter.clauseSE: I understand Trafikverket’s April letter recommended a TCMV “no” unless the speed-offset is removed.
opening: I am a resident of {name} writing about Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised). It is a SAE Level 2 driver-assistance system. The driver remains legally responsible.

On 10 April 2026 the Dutch RDW granted a provisional EU type-approval under Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2018/858. Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark and Belgium have since accepted that approval on their own territory under Article 39(5). The Dutch certificate is not an EU-wide approval. Other Member States may accept it. They are not obliged to.
closing: These approvals are provisional. If the Commission refuses authorisation, they can be unwound six months later. Delay alone does not revoke them. That is why a clear yes at TCMV matters now, not after a later rewrite of UN Regulation No. 171.

RDW tested the system itself for more than 3,000 hours before issuing the file. Tesla has since published company figures of 5.2× fewer collisions over 65 million kilometres in the five approved countries (10 April–26 July 2026). Those are Tesla’s numbers, not an independent audit. I am not asking you to take marketing slides on trust. I am asking you to finish the review and say in public what {name} will do.
askSupport: I ask you to instruct your representatives in the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles to support Commission authorisation of the implementing act. A qualified majority needs 15 Member States and 65% of the EU population. A vote is widely expected in October 2026. {name} has already accepted this file. I am not asking you to recognise it again. I am asking you to vote yes, so a Commission refusal does not start the six-month unwind of the approvals we already have.
Please tell me how {name} will vote at TCMV.
askRecognise: I ask you to do two things. First, accept the Dutch provisional approval for use in {name}, so that compatible Hardware 4 vehicles can use the approved EU build here. Second, instruct your representatives in the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles to support Commission authorisation of the implementing act. A qualified majority needs 15 Member States and 65% of the EU population. A vote is widely expected in October 2026.
Please tell me whether {name} will recognise the Dutch file nationally, and how you will vote at TCMV.
askRecogniseDE: I ask you to instruct your representatives in the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles to support Commission authorisation of the implementing act. A qualified majority needs 15 Member States and 65% of the EU population. A vote is widely expected in October 2026. I understand {clause}. I am not asking you to pretend a national Article 39(5) recognition is already your stated path. I am asking for a public yes at TCMV.
Please tell me how {name} will vote at TCMV.
askRecogniseES: I ask you to instruct your representatives in the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles to support Commission authorisation of the implementing act. A qualified majority needs 15 Member States and 65% of the EU population. A vote is widely expected in October 2026. I understand {clause}. I am not asking you to pretend a national Article 39(5) recognition is already your stated path. I am asking for a public yes at TCMV.
Please tell me how {name} will vote at TCMV.
askOpposed: I am not asking you to recognise the current product as it stands. I ask you to take a public position on the TCMV vote expected in October 2026 — a qualified majority needs 15 Member States and 65% of the EU population — and to say what would turn a no into a yes.
Please tell me how {name} will vote at TCMV.
letter.askOpposedFR: {clause} I ask you to revisit that position, or at least to support a Commission act that would let a supervised, Level 2 system operate under clear EU conditions.
letter.askOpposedSE: {clause} If that is still Sweden’s view, please say so in public and say what change would turn it into a yes. A silent no at TCMV is the outcome I want you to avoid.
